title: Rosalind and the House
premise: Jude Ravensworth, a meticulous property surveyor, arrives at Hollowmere House to appraise it for its last resident, the dying Edith Vane — but the house documents him back, its mirrors lagging one second behind reality and slowly revealing a room that shouldn't exist. He discovers the founders built the house as a vessel for a ritual of preservation: it keeps what is loved by consuming what remembers it. As Jude falls for Edith's estranged granddaughter Callum-free caretaker, Wren, he must choose between completing the founders' interrupted rite to free the house's trapped residents or letting it collapse with Edith's signature. In the end Jude finishes the ritual not as written but inverted — offering his own documented memories instead of Wren's — releasing the dead, saving Edith's final days, and walking out of Hollowmere with blank pages where his past used to be, held upright by Wren's voice.
about_author: Marguerite Sandoval is the pen name of a former archival clerk from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing deeds to houses that no longer exist. Her fiction explores the horror of paperwork done perfectly.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Jude Ravensworth's POV. He arrives at Hollowmere House with instruments, forms, and a habit of photographing everything twice. The house is immaculate in ways that unsettle him — dust refuses to settle on certain sills. Emotional beat: professional calm masking a first flicker of being observed.

chapters.title: Edith Vane Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Jude meets Edith, the last resident, who is lucid about everything except why she won't sign the sale papers. She asks him strange questions: whether he loves anyone, whether he writes things down. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: duty meeting an old woman's quiet desperation.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Wren, the live-in caretaker, shows Jude the east wing. In a hallway mirror, his reflection moves a beat behind him. He tests it scientifically; the lag holds. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: rational confidence beginning to crack against evidence he can measure but not explain.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She has kept the house for six years without pay beyond room and board, bound by a promise to her grandmother Edith. Watching Jude document everything, she feels both contempt and longing. Emotional beat: loneliness recognizing a fellow keeper of records.

chapters.title: The Founders' File
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Jude finds the original survey of Hollowmere — drawn by a surveyor whose handwriting matches his own. The plans show a thirteenth room that doesn't exist. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance, as if the house chose him long ago.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Keep
chapters.summary: At night the mirrors show rooms as they were decades ago: a family at dinner, faces Jude recognizes from portraits. One figure always looks directly out. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: voyeuristic guilt — he is watching the dead, and they know it.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession, Partially
chapters.summary: Edith tells Jude her husband signed the papers forty years ago and was 'absorbed into the upkeep.' She believes refusing to sign keeps him anchored somewhere kind. POV: Edith via Jude's recorded interview. Emotional beat: love weaponized into refusal.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirror delay grows to three seconds, then five. Jude's own reflection begins acting independently — finishing gestures he abandons. Wren admits she stopped using mirrors years ago. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror of being rehearsed by something wearing his shape.

chapters.title: Rite of Preservation
chapters.summary: Jude deciphers the founders' ledger hidden in the survey drawings: a ritual to feed the house a willing memory-bearer each generation, keeping loved ones preserved inside forever. It was never finished. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: horrified understanding that the house is mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Callum-Free
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she had a brother, Callum, who tried to burn the house down at nineteen; the house took him instead, and Edith made Wren promise to stay so Callum wouldn't be alone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as a cage disguised as devotion.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Jude realizes his obsessive notes aren't just habit — the house has been reading them, learning him through his own records. Every page he's written is a page it owns. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the archivist discovering his archive testifies against him.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Room
chapters.summary: Following the founders' measurements, Jude finds the door to the missing room behind the pantry wall — warm to the touch, breathing faintly. Inside are shelves of ledgers, each bearing a resident's name. His name is already on one, half-filled. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: predestination closing like a trap.

chapters.title: Interlude: What Callum Saw
chapters.summary: A chapter from inside the house itself — the preserved consciousness of Callum, aware, loving, unable to leave, watching Wren sleep through the mirrors. Emotional beat: tenderness without agency; captivity as an act of care.

chapters.title: Wren Decides to Leave
chapters.summary: Wren packs a bag, ready to break her promise and let the house fall with Edith's signature. But Edith collapses, and the mirrors all turn toward Wren at once. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt versus survival, the promise tightening.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The house speaks through Edith briefly, lucid and terrible: finish the ritual, give it a bearer, and everyone inside goes free — or refuse, and it takes Wren when the papers finally sign themselves. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Reading Callum's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude reads Callum's half-finished ledger and finds the flaw in the founders' rite: it demands a memory-bearer given by another, but nothing forbids a volunteer. He tells no one. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Last Night at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren spend an evening honestly — she shows him the garden Callum planted, he burns his duplicate photographs, and they admit what's growing between them. Neither says what he's planning. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love arriving precisely when it will cost most.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: Edith, near death, finally signs — and the pens in the house write on their own, the sale papers filling with names. The mirrors stop lagging entirely; reflections step out of sync completely. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: point of no return, the house fully awake.

chapters.title: Into the Middle of It
chapters.summary: Jude enters the thirteenth room and begins the rite, writing himself into the ledger while the house pulls at his memories through every mirror at once. Wren realizes what he's doing and fights her way to him. POV: Jude, fraying. Emotional beat: climax — self-erasure as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Inverted Rite
chapters.summary: Together Jude and Wren rewrite the final line: instead of surrendering memories to be kept, he offers them to be released — his own included. The ledgers ignite, the mirrors shatter outward, and Callum and the preserved dead pass through the glass and end. POV: Wren holding Jude. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: The house stands ordinary, mortal, dust settling everywhere at last. Edith dies peacefully two days later, calling her husband's name once, smiling. Jude survives but remembers almost nothing — his notebooks are blank except for Wren's name. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Appraised Anew
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wren reads to Jude from a journal she kept of their time together, rebuilding his memory aloud. He doesn't recall loving her yet — but he asks her to keep reading. Somewhere, a new mirror fogs. POV: shared. Emotional beat: resolution — memory can be lost and still be chosen again.
